runner: uv run --with pytest --with numpy --with pandas pytest tests/ -q
notes: Binary assertions per CLAUDE.md Rule #6. Unlike content skills these are NOT LLM-graded — each assertion is a deterministic pytest in tests/test_markov_regime.py that passes or fails. Re-run after model or dependency upgrades (Rule #13). The assertions lock the math claims README.md and SKILL.md make.

cases.prompt: Build the transition matrix for a synthetic bull/bear/sideways series.

assertions.check: Every observed row of P sums to 1 and all entries are in [0,1]
P[i,j] equals count(i->j)/count(i->*) — a plain MLE estimate
pi @ P == pi, pi >= 0, and pi sums to 1
pi matches a row of P^512 (Chapman-Kolmogorov convergence)

cases.prompt: Run the walk-forward backtest and verify it does not peek at the future.

assertions.check: The O(n) running-counts path is bit-identical to an O(n^2) from-scratch rebuild that only ever reads labels[:t] — proving both no-lookahead and the 'bit-identical' claim
Too little data yields NaN Sharpe and zero trades, no crash

cases.prompt: Label regimes and emit the signal.

assertions.check: Labels use SIMPLE rolling return vs ±threshold (matching the Pine indicator); a clean +8%/-8% move produces Bull/Bear labels
signal == P(bull) - P(bear) and is bounded to [-1, 1]

cases.prompt: Load a user CSV and emit the JSON contract.

assertions.check: load_csv falls back to the single numeric column when no named close column exists
analyze() emits every field documented in SKILL.md's JSON table
